chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The one upon whom is obligated the ransom of a hunted prey that he caught while in Ihram, if he was a pilgrim of Hajj, he should sacrifice his offering which is obligated upon him at Mina; and if he was a pilgrim of Umrah, he should sacrifice at Mecca, facing the Kaaba.'

key_terms.مُحْرِم: one in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: Where should a pilgrim sacrifice the ransom for a hunted animal?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific geographic locations for offering the ransom (fidya) sacrifice based on the pilgrim's status, distinguishing between the Hajj pilgrim who slaughters at Mina and the Umrah pilgrim who does so in Mecca facing the Kaaba. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the precise execution of ritual obligations tied to the sanctity of the holy sites. The ruling underscores the continuity of the Meccan rites while highlighting the distinct procedural requirements for each pilgrimage type.
